done_when: Forge's GitHub reads retry an unreadable or server-error answer a few times with a short pause before giving up, and then say plainly that GitHub didn't answer and to rerun; answers GitHub refuses on purpose (not found, no permission) are not retried; a command test with a faked gh covers one bad answer then a good one (close carries on) and a lasting outage (plain stop)

findings.body: An interrupted response body still stops after one attempt. Go's [HTTP body reader](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/golang/go/master/src/net/http/transfer.go) returns `unexpected EOF` when a response ends before its declared length, and gh's [GraphQL reader](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cli/go-gh/trunk/pkg/api/graphql_client.go) propagates that error. With nonzero exit, empty stdout and that stderr, neither unreadable detection nor either decoder-error substring matches, so this helper returns immediately without retrying or producing the plain outage/rerun message. Other JSON syntax errors, such as `invalid character '<' after object key:value pair`, also escape these two substring checks. This affects PR reads, check/protection reads and release lookups through the shared helper; `src/forge/close.py:521–528` consequently raises the original command error. Extend unreadable-response recognition while preserving intentional refusals, and cover recovery and exhaustion through the faked-gh command tests. The supplied decoder cases use only the already-matched phrase and pass with this gap present.
findings.title: Not done: Forge's GitHub reads retry an unreadable or server-error answer a few times with a short pause before giving up

why: One unreadable GitHub answer (an HTML error page: 'invalid character < looking for beginning of value') stops forge close outright outside the checks wait, so a GitHub blip costs a whole rerun (reported by a client session on v1.2.8)
